I'm testing distance from both gripper and button as possible ordering factors, but neither matches which cube gets picked first across episodes. I'll just settle on treating the order as whatever sequence the highlighted areas appear in the observation text, without forcing a strict geometric rule.

Testing largest-y doesn't hold up either. I don't think there's a reliable ordering rule here, so I'll just go with picking the first cube in the list, assuming the annotator orders the list by actual pick sequence in the recording.

For memory fields, I'm defining a button_pressed yes/no flag, and a pending_cubes field holding an ordered list of positions for cubes still needing to be picked, written once highlighted areas appear and removed once a cube is fully placed.

I'll use whichever cube position is observed closest to that highlighted area at the time, and follow the subgoal logic: start at A, remain there if no button press or highlights are detected yet, otherwise...

Once execution shows the button pressed, I record the highlighted areas and pick the first pending cube. If the gripper is holding a cube, the subgoal is C; if empty with the button pressed and pending cubes remain, it's B at the first pending cube; otherwise fall back to A.
